metaTitle: Longtail Travel: Thailand by water and by season
metaDescription: Private journeys in Thailand planned along its water and its seasons: Bangkok's khlongs, the cool north and the right coast for your month.

intro.title: We plan Thailand along its water, and we start with the month.
intro.text: The longtail is the narrow wooden boat with an engine on a long pole. It works the canals of Bangkok, the Mekong in the north and the shallows of the Andaman. We named the company after it because it goes where Thailand is actually lived. Then we let the season choose the coast.

regions.title: Places.
regions.text: Eleven places, from the khlongs of Bangkok to the quiet end of the eastern Gulf. Each one with the months we would go, and the water we would follow.

coasts.title: Two coasts. Two monsoons.
coasts.meta: Andaman, Gulf and the north, month by month
coasts.text: The Andaman coast is dry from about November to April. The Gulf is driest from February to August. Choose your month and we'll show you which way to go.

editorial.title: Watched, not ridden.
editorial.text: We don't book elephant riding or bathing. We book places where you watch from a distance, and we visit villages as guests, with a guide from the community.

faq.title: Questions before you board.
faq.text: Still unsure? Write to us and a real person will answer, usually within two working days.

items.q: Which coast should I choose for my month?
items.a: Broadly, the Andaman coast (Krabi, Koh Yao Noi, Koh Lanta) is best from November to April, and the Gulf (Samui, Phangan) from February to August. October and November are the most awkward months. Our two-coasts picker shows each month.

Many nationalities can enter Thailand for tourism without a visa for a limited stay, and the length has changed recently. Check the official guidance for your passport before you book, and complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card online before you land.

items.q: How much can we fit into two weeks?
items.a: Three places, perhaps four. Bangkok, one region of the north or Khao Sok, and one coast. More than that and you spend the holiday in transit.
Only at observation-based sanctuaries we have checked, where you watch the elephants from a distance. We do not book riding, bathing, shows or painting.

items.q: What does the rainy season really mean?
items.a: Usually a heavy shower in the afternoon and green, quiet landscapes. On the exposed coast, though, the sea can be rough for weeks and some boats and hotels close. We plan around it.
Send an enquiry. We reply with a first route by email, then a written proposal with prices for your dates. Nothing is booked until you confirm and pay the deposit stated in the proposal.
